page: Microsoft Azure D48plds_v5 is an ARM-based server instance belonging to the DPLDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 1843 GB, and the instance supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark data reveals a contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 85051.53 and a Geekbench software compilation score of 39975.0, both placing in the top 25 percent. Redis SET operations are also strong at 62.24 million operations per second. Conversely, single-core performance is relatively weak, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1117.0 and a single-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 8.92 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth is moderate, reaching 176.14 GB/sec for large-block read operations.

Given the 1-to-2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, this instance is structured for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading ensure predictable execution, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for scale-out workloads like software compilation, web serving, and database operations. However, the lack of advanced vector extensions and poor large-model LLM prompt processing make it less suitable for heavy AI or machine learning workloads. It is best fit for multi-threaded applications, static web serving, and containerized microservices.

It features 96.0 GB of memory and 1843 GB of local storage. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, this instance provides dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading. Benchmarks indicate strong multi-core performance, highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core score of 85051.53 and high software compilation speeds. However, single-core performance is weaker, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1117.0. Lacking AVX and AMX extensions, it is not designed for heavy vector math. Qualitatively, the server offers a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded scale-out workloads, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from local storage and high core density rather than high memory-per-core ratios.
